In the nonresonant case gcd(pa,qb)=1; a common-frequency translation and CRT put every frequency in one of two coordinate axes, but their cross-differences cannot be zeros. Each axis permits at most p or q pairwise distinct residue classes, and q is attained. The precise q-maximizer description follows from equality. In either resonance, pq explicit pairwise-orthogonal exponentials exist and coprimality proves pq distinct support points, giving a basis and a matching dimension ceiling.
